status: PREPARED BY D-198 — IMAGE CALLS AUTHORISED ONLY BY D-199 (base-figure-calls-v1.json: A, reserve B) — NO BASE FIGURE EXISTS
purpose: The target and the acceptance contract for ONE shared Northstar-style base figure in neutral, close-fitting base clothing, with continuous arms, legs and feet, so short and open clothing forms become possible. It replaces D-197's clothed base as the goal; D-197 stays a documented experiment.

source.role: the only image input of the future call and the geometric reference of every gate

head.rule: The existing allowed head is kept: the Northstar-based R3 head stack (D-188/D-193/D-194, in master coordinates). The generated figure contributes only the body below the neck seam; the head is never taken from the generated image.
head.recomposition: r3-northstar-figure.mjs bodyLayer(candidate, bald head, spec.body) — the D-194 seam rule, unchanged; no painting, no warp

anything derived from H1 (D-133 TRANSITION rows, r3-head-g1v3-v1.png)
the R2 base (a different figure, silhouette IoU 0.77)
pose: Northstar v2's front-facing neutral standing pose, centre axis, scale and placement; arms hanging at the sides, hands open beside the thighs, feet on one ground line.
anchorsFrom: northstar-wardrobe.mjs anchors() on Northstar v2 (measured, not typed): neck seam 440, shoulders 499, sleeve end 787, wrists 835/849, waistband 790, crotch 849, shoe top 1348/1349, ground 1488, centre 512

kneeY.kind: ESTIMATE — the jeans hide the knees; midpoint of crotch 849 and ankle 1367; used for the prompt wording and review only, never as a gate

targets.why: The base garments are the MINIMUM coverage every later item must hide. So the base top ends at the natural waist (tops may be waist-length, not t-shirt-length), the base shorts end at mid-thigh (shorts and skirts may be that short), and the neckline is a moderate round neck. The ranges also keep both base garments inside Northstar's own tee and jeans, so D-197's three default items can dress the new base back into the original Northstar look (BF15).

storage.rule: D-127 §2 applies unchanged to the generated figure: a drawn figure in close-fitting base clothing is never tracked in the public repository and never placed under assets/. Raw output, recomposed figure and its base-garment layers live outside both clones (e.g. C:\Users\Bruger\Documents\DenSejeApp-artefacts\) with full provenance: sha256, byte count, request id, model, parameters, input order, prompt hash, timestamp.
storage.tracked: only this spec, the prompt, the tools and their tests, sha256 values and measured numbers
storage.runtime: OPEN OWNER DECISION O1 — which separated skin layers (arms, hands, legs, feet, neck and shoulders; never the base garments and never the regions they cover) may later be tracked and deployed

baseClothingStrategy.rule: The base garments are AUTHORING MATERIAL ONLY. They define the mandatory minimum coverage of the top and bottom categories and are never shipped or shown.
baseClothingStrategy.runtime: The runtime body layer leaves the base garments' regions EMPTY (transparent). Every outfit must contain a top and a bottom whose opaque pixels cover the base top and base shorts regions (plus 1 px) completely; the resolver renders complete-or-null, so a figure without them never renders.
baseClothingStrategy.hidden: Under every top and bottom: the top covers the base top, the bottom covers the base shorts.
baseClothingStrategy.replaced: There is nothing to replace at runtime: the base garments are absent, the item takes their place.
baseClothingStrategy.extraction: During item extraction the base figure WITH its base garments is the 'behind' picture, so an item is measured against exactly what it must hide.

classes.original-kept: the R3 head stack above the neck seam — existing allowed pixels, never regenerated
classes.original-reference: Northstar's visible neck, forearms and hands — redrawn by the generator and measured against the original (silhouette gates); the original pixels are not pasted back unless a later join check passes (D-131 found clearly unacceptable joins when pixel-identical v2 arms met generated upper arms)
classes.reconstructed: body that Northstar hides and the base shows: shoulders, upper arms, thighs, knees, shins, ankles, feet
classes.new: the base garments (base top, base shorts) — new authoring material, never shipped
classes.removed: Northstar clothing outside the new limbs (the excess width of sleeves, jeans and sneakers) — transparent in the base

provenance.map: before the call: provenanceExpected() from Northstar's decomposition; after the call: provenanceMeasured() from the registered candidate

visualCriteria: V1 The same character: Northstar's painted style, line weight, soft shading and colours; the figure reads as Northstar without clothes over it, not as a new drawing style.
V2 Child-friendly and neutral: no nudity, no anatomical detail, no navel, no muscle definition, no body emphasis; the base garments read as plain sportswear.
V3 Natural joins at neck, shoulders, elbows, wrists, knees and ankles: no seams, steps, colour breaks or doubled outlines where reconstructed skin meets the original.
V4 Proportions consistent with the clothed Northstar: limbs neither thinner nor thicker than the clothing implies; both sides symmetric where Northstar is.
V5 Hands and feet in Northstar's style; simple stylised toes; feet flat on the ground line.
V6 Base garments plain: one colour each, no logos, text, patterns, folds or decoration.
V7 At app sizes (hub 110×165, quiz 52×78) the figure reads cleanly; no halo, no fringe on the real surface.
V8 Dressed back in D-197's default items, it is visually the original Northstar.
automaticVersusVisual: BF1–BF15 are automatic and binding; a fail rejects the candidate, and nothing is retouched to pass them. V1–V8 need the owner's eyes; the gates cannot judge style, anatomy, child-appropriateness or the quality of a join, and a pass on BF never substitutes for them.
